title: Irrationality of ∛3 via Eisenstein Criterion
question: Can the Eisenstein irreducibility criterion be used to give a structural algebraic proof that ∛3 is irrational? Show X³-3 is irreducible over ℤ via Eisenstein at p=3, transfer to ℚ via Gauss's lemma, then derive irrationality.

insights: Eisenstein at p=3 for X³-3: all 5 conditions are trivial except ¬(9∣3) which uses Int.le_of_dvd
IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast is the Gauss lemma transfer in Mathlib
Real.rpow_mul proves (3^(1/3))^3 = 3 by the chain y=1/3, z=3 → y*z=1
algebraMap ℚ ℝ injective argument lifts rational roots to real: apply_fun then aeval_algebraMap_apply
